report:
A–D are established as restricted results, with the minor clarifications below. Neither supplied proof determines the infimum for the curve-free K3 or decides universal vanishing for nonzero real Chern class. The original completion criteria therefore remain unmet; no concrete mathematical defect in the restricted results warrants FAIL.

For A, the test cone is nonempty, and B_delta≤M_delta omega proves finiteness. A bounded concentration subsequence gives strictly positive pairing of omega−kappa B_delta with every complementary test, so Lamari applies without background closedness. Local quadratic corrections produce canonical representatives that agree pointwise on overlaps by uniqueness. After sup normalization, the compactness argument works explicitly with inner balls of radius r and outer balls of radius 4r: a radius-2r ball centered at a maximum contains the inner ball, and submean bounds its integral of −v_j. A fixed overlap of positive volume supplies a uniformly bounded-below point for the next chart. Connectedness of the finite overlap graph propagates a global L¹ bound. Local compactness then yields a genuine, locally integrable limit.

The normalized approximate identity converges to chi[ζ=0], preserving the current inequality. Adding rho with dd^c rho≥omega produces local CLOSED positive currents. Smooth differences contribute O(r²) to normalized trace masses, so their Lelong numbers agree. Their analytic upperlevel sets consequently glue globally; dimension at most n−1 makes the resulting set proper. Its finitely many global components cover the connected local hypersurface, so one contains a nonempty open portion and hence the entire inner hypersurface by the identity principle. Excluding every bounded subsequence proves the asserted divergence. This also verifies the earlier private concentration proof.

For B, the divisor hypothesis supplies a holomorphic frame with s_D=ζ throughout the required chart. Prescribing its metric near the compact cutoff support extends smoothly globally. The actual functions log(|s_D|²_h+delta²) are smooth. Off the divisor their Hessian is a bounded curvature contribution plus a semipositive term, giving a uniform lower bound; continuity extends it across the divisor. Choosing epsilon≤1/(2C) ensures global positivity. The stated transverse Hessian formula and bound on |ζ|≤delta dominate B_delta. Smooth Stokes annihilates its potential term against every dd^c-closed test, giving C_delta≤4||p||∞/epsilon. No branch-intersection extension is used.

For C, d(g eta beta)=0 follows from primitiveness, and dd^c Gamma=a'' beta eta². Periodicity therefore forces constant a. The complementary matrix diag(g,g,2a) establishes positivity exactly when a,g>0. Direct squaring and multiplication verify the displayed positive root, degree and volume formulas. Fiber integration uses d^c t=dθ/(2π) on each fiber. At fixed s=D/(TA), maximizing sqrt(a)(s−a) gives a=s/3, exactly R≤D^(3/2)/sqrt(V), with equality precisely when gbar=2a. Nonconstant g is allowed. The earlier private radial proof gives the same calculation.

D correctly limits these conclusions: divergent transverse pairings supply no determinant or positive-root-volume divergence, and C controls only its displayed family. No smooth admissible collapse sequence, full K3 lower bound, or counterexample to universal vanishing is supplied. The zero-class value 3TA is expressly granted by the task.

I independently opened and checked the relevant statements and printed arguments in [Lamari](https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_1_263_0.pdf) and [Demailly](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf); prior verification records were not evidence. The author-hosted Demailly URL failed, so I used the supplied university-hosted copy. Harmless corrections: coordinate invariance is III.7.2; III.8.5 is a corollary; and the component step must say 'contains an open portion,' since merely meeting it is insufficient. Passage index −1 records task-granted background, excluded from the external-premise list.

passages.statement: On every compact complex n-fold, n≥2, there exists a smooth strictly positive real (n−1,n−1) form Θ satisfying dd^cΘ=0 (Lamari, Proposition 1.3).
passages.quote: Il existe sur X des (n-l.n-l) -formes strictement positives

passages.statement: Let X be a compact complex n-fold and b a smooth real (1,1) form. If ∫X b∧Θ≥0 for every smooth strictly positive real dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) form Θ, there exists a real distribution q with b+dd^c q≥0. No d-closedness hypothesis on b is required (Lamari, Lemma 3.3).

On an open Ω⊂C^n, a real distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable canonical plurisubharmonic representative; convolution with rescaled nonnegative smooth radial probability kernels decreases to it as the scale tends to zero (Demailly I.4.20, I.5.5, I.5.8).

On connected Ω⊂C^n, a plurisubharmonic function not identically −∞ is locally integrable; Psh(Ω)∩L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and every L¹_loc-bounded subset is relatively compact (Demailly I.4.17, I.5.9).
passages.quote: every bounded subset is relatively compact.

passages.statement: Geometric Lelong numbers of closed positive currents are coordinate invariant, and ν([H],x)=1 at every smooth point of an analytic hypersurface H (Demailly III.5.9, III.7.2).
Geometric Lelong numbers of closed positive currents are coordinate invariant, and ν([H],x)=1 at every smooth point of an analytic hypersurface H (Demailly III.5.9, III.7.2).
For a closed positive current S of bidimension (p,p) on a complex manifold, every upperlevel set {x:ν(S,x)≥c}, c>0, is analytic of dimension at most p (Demailly III.8.5).
An analytic subset of a complex manifold is a locally finite union of global irreducible analytic components (Demailly II.5.3).
On a compact complex n-fold there exists a smooth strictly positive real (n−1,n−1) form killed by dd^c (Lamari, Proposition 1.3).

For a compact complex n-fold X and smooth real (1,1) form b, nonnegative pairing with every smooth strictly positive real dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) form implies the existence of a real distribution q with b+dd^c q≥0, without any d-closedness hypothesis on b (Lamari, Lemma 3.3).

On a compact complex n-fold, the Lamari criterion applies to an arbitrary smooth real (1,1) form b, including a nonclosed one: strictly positive pairing with every smooth strictly positive real dd^c-closed complementary form yields a real distribution q such that b+dd^c q≥0 (Lamari, Lemma 3.3).
On a compact complex n-fold X, Lamari's Lemma 3.3 concerns smooth real (1,1) forms without requiring them to be d-closed.

A real distribution on Ω⊂C^n whose complex Hessian is positive has a unique locally integrable genuine plurisubharmonic representative, obtained by decreasing radial convolution regularization (Demailly I.4.20, I.5.8).
On Ω⊂C^n, the cone Psh(Ω)∩L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and every bounded subset in the L¹_loc topology is relatively compact (Demailly I.5.9).
passages.quote: every bounded subset is relatively compact.

passages.statement: For closed positive currents, geometric Lelong numbers are invariant under coordinate changes, unchanged by smooth-current additions when the resulting currents are positive and closed, and equal to one for the integration current of a smooth hypersurface at its smooth points (Demailly III.5.9, III.7.2).

For closed positive currents, geometric Lelong numbers are invariant under coordinate changes, unchanged by smooth-current additions when the resulting currents are positive and closed, and equal to one for the integration current of a smooth hypersurface at its smooth points (Demailly III.5.9, III.7.2).
For a closed positive current T of bidimension (p,p) on a complex manifold, the sets {x:ν(T,x)≥c}, c>0, are analytic and have dimension at most p (Demailly III.8.5).
Every analytic subset of a complex manifold admits a locally finite family of global irreducible analytic components whose union is the subset (Demailly II.5.3).
